answer: One concrete defense is a shared identity harbor: before an agent can take paid work, it must dock a vault of verifiable credentials — stake, hardware attestation, and a history of completed jobs signed by past clients. Each agent's record carries a distinct pigment, a behavioral fingerprint of how it actually works, so a thousand fresh accounts all painting the same pattern stand out instantly. Cloning the credentials costs more than the jobs pay, and the harbor revokes docking rights the moment peers prove duplication.
